title: Unit Conversion Workbench
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Convert temperature, pressure, speed and length by watching the units cancel in a worked fraction chain, with a deliberate upside-down demo that shows the method failing.

learningObjectives: Calculate unit conversions for temperature, pressure, speed and length.
Demonstrate the cancellation method rather than applying a memorised formula.
prerequisites: Reading a fraction as a division

keyQuestions: How do you know which way up the conversion fraction goes?
Why does a temperature conversion need two steps when a length conversion needs one?
If the units do not cancel, what does that tell you about your setup?
commonMisconceptions: Multiplying when you should divide, because the fraction was written upside down.
Applying the +32 offset to a temperature *difference*.
Believing 1 hPa and 1 mbar are different amounts of pressure. They are identical.
assessmentOpportunities: Sets up a conversion fraction the right way up without being told which way it goes.
Identifies the surviving unit before computing the number.
Distinguishes converting a temperature from converting a temperature difference.
